title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: f: X -> S is a family of complex-analytic varieties, with relative de Rham complex Omega^*_{X/S}. On the previous page Grothendieck sets Phi = f_*(Z Omega^1_{X/S}) / d f_*(O_X), the first relative de Rham cohomology in the affine or Stein-fibre sense. Phi carries the integrable Gauss-Manin connection, obtained via the Cartan formula. Given sections omega_i of Phi and differential operators D_i on S (acting through Gauss-Manin), a Picard-Fuchs-type relation is condition (7): sum D_i omega_i = 0 in Phi.

The aim is to show that (7) implies the corresponding linear differential equation (3) for periods: sum_i D_{i,s} \int_{Z_s} omega_{i,s} = 0 for every horizontal family of cycles Z_s.

Method, under the auxiliary hypothesis that X/S itself carries an integrable connection (a stratification, i.e. locally a product):
- Lift each D_i to an operator \bar D_i on Omega^*_X that commutes with d_{X/S}.
- Put varpi = sum \bar D_i omega_i, which is again a relative closed form. Its class in Phi is sum D_i omega_i, equation (9).
- So (7) says that, locally over S, varpi = d phi with phi a function on X, equation (10).
- The key identity is differentiation under the integral sign over horizontal cycles, (12): D_s \int_{Z_s} omega_s = \int_{Z_s} \bar D_s omega_s. This holds for any differential operator D on S and any relative closed holomorphic form omega. Closedness makes the period holomorphic in s, which gives the left side a meaning.
- Summing gives (11): sum_i D_{is} \int omega_{is} = \int_{Z_s} varpi = \int_{Z_s} d phi = \int_{\partial Z_s} phi = 0, because Z_s is a cycle.

The next page proves (12) without the product hypothesis. It cuts Z_{s0} into small paths with horizontally transported endpoints, works on small paths where omega = d phi locally, and derives D_s \int_{a(s)}^{b(s)} omega_s = \int_{a(s)}^{b(s)} (\bar D omega)_s.

In short, this is an expository derivation that periods are solutions of the Picard-Fuchs equations defined by the Gauss-Manin connection.
errors: Assuming X/S carries an integrable connection (so that the D_i lift globally on fibres to operators \bar D_i commuting with d_{X/S}) is very restrictive: it essentially means local triviality of the family. In general the lifts exist only locally on X. The rigorous route is either the Katz-Oda construction or the path-cutting argument on the next page, which uses only local primitives. As written on this page, the argument is a special-case heuristic.
Minor: 'localement au dessus de S' must mean on f^{-1}(U) for small open U in S. phi has to be defined on a neighbourhood of the whole cycle Z_s, not just locally on X, for the Stokes step to work.

The reference '(3)' here points to the Picard-Fuchs relation on periods stated earlier. The next page reuses the label (3) for the path-integral formula, so the equation numbering is inconsistent across pages.

ideas.what: Gauss-Manin connection on relative de Rham cohomology f_*(Z Omega^1_{X/S})/d f_* O_X and Picard-Fuchs relations sum D_i omega_i = 0
ideas.usually_credited_to: Manin (1958); Grothendieck (1966 letter on de Rham cohomology); Katz-Oda (1968)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (Publ. IHES 29, 1966); Katz-Oda 1968 credits Grothendieck

ideas.what: Periods over horizontal cycles satisfy the Picard-Fuchs equation, via differentiation under the integral sign D \int_{Z_s} omega = \int_{Z_s} \bar D omega and Stokes
ideas.modern_name: Periods as horizontal solutions / compatibility of Gauss-Manin with the period pairing
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Picard, Fuchs, Manin); formalized by Katz (1970), Deligne (1970)
ideas.where_published: Standard; appears in Katz 'Nilpotent connections and the monodromy theorem' and Deligne 'Équations différentielles à points singuliers réguliers'

ideas.what: Lifting differential operators on S to operators on Omega^*_X commuting with d_{X/S} when X/S is stratified
ideas.modern_name: Lifting via a connection / stratification of X over S (Cartan homotopy formula)

deep.surprise_reason: The page carefully derives the classical fact that periods over horizontal cycles satisfy the Picard-Fuchs equations coming from the Gauss-Manin connection. This is well established in the literature (Manin, Katz-Oda, Katz, Deligne), and the page contains nothing beyond the standard argument.
transcription_corrections: (9): '$\sum D_i\omega_i = \varpi'$ dans $\mathcal{P}$' should read '... = \varpi' dans \Phi': the class of varpi in Phi. The word 'dans' is crossed out, or nearly so.
(10): '$\varphi \in \Gamma(X,\mathcal{C}_X)$' is most likely $\Gamma(X,\mathcal{O}_X)$, given the definition Phi = f_*Z\Omega^1/d f_*\mathcal{O}_X.
In '(10) \varpi (= \sum \overline{D}_i\omega_i)' the index under \overline{D} is overwritten in ink, perhaps a struck 'D_\xi' corrected to 'D_i'.
'(1\lambda)' and '(1\mathbb{Z})' in the image are (11) and (12).
'$\int_{\partial Z_s}\varphi = 0$ puisque $\partial Z_s = 0$' matches the image reasonably; the handwriting reads roughly '\int_{\partial Z_s}\varphi = 0 puisque \partial Z_s = 0'.
The insertion above 'forme' reads 'holomorphe fermée' (relative closed holomorphic form); the bracketed comment follows.
